members.name: Jacqueline Halbig
members.bio: Founder and principal partner of Sovereign Global Solutions. She served at the White House as Associate Director of Faith-Based and Community Initiatives and held senior posts at the U.S. Departments of Labor and Health and Human Services. She is a founding board member of the National Catholic Prayer Breakfast.

members.name: John Klink
members.bio: Former lead negotiator for the Holy See Mission to the United Nations and past President of the International Catholic Migration Commission.

members.name: William Saunders
members.bio: Director of the Center for Human Rights at The Catholic University of America, where he also directs the Program in Human Rights and co-directs the Center for Religious Liberty at the Columbus School of Law. He is President of the Fellowship of Catholic Scholars and a graduate of Harvard Law School.

members.name: Joseph Cella
members.bio: United States Ambassador to Fiji, Kiribati, Nauru, Tonga, and Tuvalu from 2019 to 2021. He is a co-founder of the National Catholic Prayer Breakfast and a founder of CatholicVote.org.

members.name: Jane Adolphe
members.bio: Professor of Law at Ave Maria School of Law, where she writes on international law and the Holy See. She advised the Secretariat of State of the Holy See under three Popes and is founder and President of the International Catholic Jurists Forum.
members.full: Dr. Adolphe is a Professor of Law at Ave Maria School of Law (AMSL), in Naples, Florida (2001 – present), who writes in the area of international law and the Holy See. She worked for three Popes: John Paul II, Benedict XVI and Francis, first, as an external legal advisor (2003-2011), then as an internal advisor (2011 – 2020), both times to the Secretariat of State, Section for Relations with States and Organizations (as it is now called). She holds a Bachelor of Arts from the University of Calgary and is a civil lawyer holding degrees in common law and civil law (B.C.L./LL.B.) from McGill University. She is qualified to practice law in the State of New York and the Province of Alberta after completing a clerkship with the Court of Appeal and Queens Bench in Calgary, Alberta, and the law firm Bennett Jones Verchere. She holds a licentiate and doctorate in canon law (J.C.L./J.C.D.) from the Pontifical University of the Holy Cross, in Rome. She was enrolled in the Postdoctoral Program with the Pontifical University of St. Thomas Aquinas, in Rome (2021-2026), with ten publications authored or edited alone or with others in the area of law; seven of them peer reviewed. She established and is President of the International Catholic Jurists Forum (ICJF), which has organized multiple international expert meetings, some resulting in books that she has co-edited (2014-present).
